source_refs.note: Unnumbered heading Universal Quantifier (for all) under 2.9, as printed (PDF 32, printed 28).

blocks.text: The universal quantifier is used to indicate that a statement is true for all objects in a given set (as shown in Figure 2.8). It is denoted by the symbol “∀”. For example, “∀x, x > 0” means “For all x, x is greater than 0.” The universal quantifier is used to make general statements about every object in a domain. It is important in mathematics and logic proofs. Using “for all” ensures that no object in the set violates the statement. This quantifier helps express rules and general truths clearly.
